lessons.title: Counting to 20

teach.intro: Counting in order helps us know exactly how many things there are.

lessons.review: Counting confidently to 20 is a big first step toward all kinds of math!

lessons.title: Addition within 10

teach.intro: Addition means putting two groups together to find how many in all.
examples: 2 + 3 means 2 things and 3 more things together

lessons.review: Addition is everywhere - counting toys, snacks, and more!

lessons.title: Subtraction within 10

teach.intro: Subtraction means taking part of a group away to see how many are left.
examples: 5 - 2 means starting with 5 and taking away 2

lessons.review: Subtraction helps you figure out what's left after using or giving something away.

lessons.title: Shapes

teach.intro: Shapes have different numbers of sides and corners.

questions.prompt: A shape with 3 sides is called a...
A shape with 4 equal sides is called a...
A shape with no corners is called a...
A shape with 2 long and 2 short sides is called a...

lessons.review: You can find shapes all around you - windows, signs, wheels, and more!

lessons.title: Comparing Numbers

teach.intro: Comparing numbers means figuring out which is more, less, or the same.

lessons.review: Comparing numbers helps you decide which group has more or less.

lessons.title: Tens and Ones

teach.intro: Numbers are made of tens and ones. The number 24 means 2 tens and 4 ones.

questions.prompt: What number is 4 tens and 2 ones?

lessons.review: Understanding tens and ones is the foundation for bigger math later!

lessons.title: Skip Counting

teach.intro: Skip counting means counting in jumps, like by 2s, 5s, or 10s, instead of one at a time.

lessons.review: Skip counting makes counting big groups much faster!

lessons.title: Addition within 20

teach.intro: Addition within 20 works just like smaller addition, just with bigger numbers.

lessons.review: Great job adding bigger numbers - you're ready for even more!

lessons.title: Measuring: Longer, Shorter, Heavier, Lighter

teach.intro: We can compare things by their size and weight.
examples: A bus is longer than a pencil
A rock is heavier than a feather

questions.prompt: Which is longer, a pencil or a bus?
Which is heavier, a feather or a rock?
Which is shorter, a mouse or an elephant?
Which holds more, a cup or a bathtub?

lessons.review: Comparing size and weight helps you describe objects around you!

lessons.title: Telling Time to the Hour

teach.intro: Clocks help us know what time it is. The short hand shows the hour.
examples: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12 = 3:00
There are 24 hours in a day
There are 60 minutes in an hour

questions.prompt: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12. What time is it?
Short hand on 7, long hand on 12. What time is it?
How many hours are in a day?
How many minutes are in an hour?

lessons.review: Now you can read a clock and know the hour!
